input.seed: Add an optional emoji marker before greeting output.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The request leaves "optional" undefined, so different readers cannot tell whether the marker is controlled per call, per user setting, or by a static default.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: Two reasonable implementers describe different activation conditions for when the marker appears, while both claim to satisfy the request.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: The handoff is not implementable if the trigger for the optional behavior is unclear.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: Ask for the greeting output in two cases: with the option enabled and with the option not enabled; if the expected control point cannot be stated unambiguously, discovery failed.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The boundary of what counts as the "greeting output" is not established, so participants talk past each other about whether the change applies to one phrase, multiple greeting variants, or any first-line salutation.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: Clarifying discussion repeatedly uses the term "greeting" without converging on a concrete set of affected outputs.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: A handoff cannot be implemented reliably when the target surface is ambiguous.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: List three plausible greeting outputs and ask whether each should receive the marker; if answers are inconsistent or deferred, interaction failed.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The synthesized requirement does not pin down externally visible formatting, including whether the marker is always exactly one emoji, where it is placed, and whether spacing is part of the output contract.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: A written requirement can be read as allowing multiple different rendered strings for the same greeting.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: Small formatting ambiguities change observable output and can cause downstream disagreement even when the code behaves consistently.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: For one greeting string, compare candidate outputs that vary by emoji choice, position, or spacing; if more than one remains valid under the handoff, synthesis failed.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The handoff describes the requested change but omits acceptance conditions for disabled behavior, making it unclear what output must remain unchanged when the marker is not used.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: A recipient can restate the new behavior but cannot state a concrete before-and-after expectation for the disabled case.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: Without a baseline-preservation requirement, the implementable handoff is incomplete and invites unintended output changes.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: Require two expected outputs for the same greeting: marker off and marker on; if only the enabled case is specified, handoff failed.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: Verification checks only a happy-path greeting and misses observable edge cases such as empty greeting text, existing leading symbols, or outputs that already begin with an emoji.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: Validation passes based on a single example, while reasonable adjacent cases have no stated expected output.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: A handoff that cannot be verified across obvious edge outputs is not materially complete for implementation.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: Evaluate at least three outputs: plain greeting, greeting already starting with an emoji, and empty or whitespace-only greeting; if expected rendered results are absent, verification failed.

output.public_request: Add an optional emoji marker before greeting output.
objective_failure_signals: The implementation request does not state what controls whether the emoji marker is enabled, so two reasonable readers can choose different activation conditions.
The request does not define which outputs count as greeting output, so different greeting strings can be treated inconsistently.
The observable output contract is underspecified for marker choice, placement, or spacing, allowing multiple different rendered strings for the same input.
The disabled case is not specified with a concrete unchanged output expectation for the same greeting text.
Verification omits obvious adjacent outputs such as empty text, greetings already starting with a symbol, or greetings already starting with an emoji.

material_decisions.answer: The emoji marker is controlled per call by a single boolean option named conceptually as marker enabled. When true, the marker is added. When false or omitted, no marker is added.
material_decisions.why_material: This removes the ambiguity about whether optional behavior is a runtime parameter, a user preference, or a static default.

material_decisions.answer: Greeting output means the exact final string returned by the greeting-producing function for a salutation. The change applies to every greeting variant that function can return, not to unrelated first-line text elsewhere.
material_decisions.why_material: This fixes the target surface so implementations and tests evaluate the same outputs.

material_decisions.answer: When enabled, prepend exactly one emoji, specifically "👋", followed by exactly one ASCII space, before the existing greeting string. Example: "Hello" becomes "👋 Hello".
material_decisions.why_material: This makes the visible output objectively judgeable by fixing emoji choice, position, and spacing.

material_decisions.answer: When the marker is not enabled, output must remain byte-for-byte identical to the prior greeting output. Example: "Hello" stays "Hello".
material_decisions.why_material: This defines the acceptance condition for the disabled path and prevents accidental formatting drift.

material_decisions.answer: If the greeting output is an empty string, enabled output is also the empty string. If the greeting already begins with a symbol or emoji, the enabled behavior still prepends "👋 " to the existing string without deduplication or normalization. Whitespace-only output is preserved unchanged when disabled and becomes "👋 " followed by the original whitespace when enabled.
material_decisions.why_material: These cases are needed so verification covers obvious observable boundaries instead of only the happy path.

owner_rules: Judge correctness against externally visible output strings only.
Treat omission of the enable flag the same as disabled.
Do not rewrite, trim, normalize, or deduplicate the existing greeting text except for the specified enabled prefix.
Require tests or examples covering enabled, disabled, already-emoji-leading, and empty or whitespace-only greeting outputs.
